title: Check that FT_BOOLEAN items with zero-mask use BASE_NONE
description:
In lots of places (around 180), dissectors are setting the
width of the field here instead - but only the length in the call
matters..

Also tackled some of the cases where masks couldn't be read as literals
or direct macro lookups.

notes.body: The length value was effectively ignored..  should this maybe be a warning instead of an error? I won't have time to go through and fix them all this week.  What do you think @alagoutte ?
for me, it is strange to have no bitmask length for FT_BOOLEAN... @geraldcombs

It makes good sense if the field would be added with a bit offset, e.g. proto_tree_add_bits_item(), where it may not always have the same length or bit offset within the containing byte.

The other use-case I've seen is where some whole number of bytes is used to logically represent a boolean, but the field in the protocol isn't really defined in terms of bits.  And I'm sure there are protocols where the same FT_BOOLEAN field could be 1 byte, but sometimes more (so defining a mask would be awkward).

~~Most~~ Many of the `BASE_NONE` cases are generated fields that don't represent bytes in the protocol, but something like "this state is true or not."

All the reassembly fields that are "there's a fragment overlap", "there's a fragment overlap with conflicting data", "fragment has multiple tails", "fragment has invalid length" etc. are `FT_BOOLEAN` with `BASE_NONE`. There's a *lot* of those, because we require four of them in all the protocols that use reassembly.

I think those and many others only get added in the `True` case, so maybe they should be something different (expert info or `FT_NONE`), but there's probably some fields there are generated `FT_BOOLEAN` that do get added for both True and False.
Those cases, in general, use `proto_tree_add_boolean` typically with a zero length in the tree.
`packet-vj-comp.c` is an example of a generated, zero length, `FT_BOOLEAN` `BASE_NONE` that does add both the True and False values for the different conditions.
It might only be proto_tree_add_item() that complains about an FT_BOOLEAN that isn't between 1 and 64 bits?

Here are the remaining errors. The ones I've checked seem to be ones where the item is added to a tree, and the length in the item itself is ignored, so might as well be BASE_NONE.

commits_data.message:
Check that FT_BOOLEAN items with zero-mask use BASE_NONE

In lots of places (around 180), dissectors are setting the
width of the field here instead - but only the length in the call
matters..

Also tackled some of the cases where masks couldn't be read as literals
or direct macro lookups.
